record.paper_title: Some open problems in mathematical relativity
record.original_question: Is the Bartnik quasi-local mass strictly positive for non-flat data, and is the Penrose quasi-local mass non-negative on reasonable data?

evidence.quote: Show the Bartnik quasi-local mass [BR6] is strictly positive for non-flat data. Show that the Penrose quasi-local mass is non-negative on reasonable data (there are examples [TP] with negative mass).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $(\Omega, g)$ be a compact, connected three-dimensional Riemannian manifold with smooth boundary $\partial\Omega$, satisfying the dominant energy condition (e.g. non-negative scalar curvature in the time-symmetric case). The Bartnik quasi-local mass of $(\Omega,g)$ is defined as
$$m_B(\Omega,g) = \inf\{ m_{\mathrm{ADM}}(M,\bar g) : (M,\bar g)\text{ is an admissible asymptotically flat extension of }(\Omega,g)\},$$
where an admissible extension is a complete asymptotically flat 3-manifold of non-negative scalar curvature, containing $(\Omega,g)$ isometrically, with no horizons enclosing $\Omega$, and $m_{\mathrm{ADM}}$ denotes the ADM mass at infinity.

The Penrose quasi-local mass is defined for a spacelike 2-surface $\Sigma$ bounding a region in a spacetime satisfying the dominant energy condition, by a kinematic-twistor / Penrose-type construction assigning a real number $m_P(\Sigma)$ that should reduce to the ADM/Bondi mass in appropriate limits.

Prove or disprove the following two statements:

(a) (Strict positivity of Bartnik mass.) If $(\Omega, g)$ is not flat (i.e., not locally isometric to a domain in Euclidean $\mathbb{R}^3$), then $m_B(\Omega,g) > 0$.

(b) (Non-negativity of Penrose mass.) For every "reasonable" spacelike 2-surface $\Sigma$ in a spacetime satisfying the dominant energy condition (e.g., $\Sigma$ a convex 2-sphere in a spacelike hypersurface with appropriate energy conditions), $m_P(\Sigma) \ge 0$.
artifact.status_search_result: Both questions remain open. For the Bartnik mass, Huisken–Ilmanen showed that vanishing implies local flatness for a related definition, but strict positivity for general non-flat data is still listed as an open conjecture in recent surveys (e.g., 2023 paper "The Bartnik quasi-local mass conjectures"). The Penrose quasi-local mass is known to admit examples with negative values (Tod), and general non-negativity on suitably restricted "reasonable" data remains unresolved.

status_evidence.title: The Bartnik quasi-local mass conjectures
status_evidence.snippet: Bartnik conjectured strict positivity of m_B; the conjecture remains a central open problem.
status_evidence.claim: Strict positivity of the Bartnik mass for non-flat data is an open conjecture.

status_evidence.title: Embeddings, immersions and the Bartnik quasi-local mass conjectures
status_evidence.snippet: Discussion of Bartnik's positivity and minimization conjectures, treating them as open problems.
status_evidence.claim: Bartnik's positivity conjecture is treated as open in the literature.
